read.thesis: Record $271B backlog (book-to-bill 1.14) and raised FY sales to $92.5-93.5B and EPS to $6.70-6.90, with Raytheon rolling book-to-bill 1.48 and five framework munitions agreements still unsigned.

capex.quote: Nearly $900 million of capital expenditures over three years at major U.S. sites to support capacity expansion for new agreements, with further investment planned.

triggers.label: FY sales guide raised $500M
triggers.quote: we're raising our full year adjusted sales outlook by $500 million to a new range of $92.5 billion to $93.5 billion
triggers.highlight: raising our full year adjusted sales outlook by $500 million

triggers.label: Record backlog $271B, up 25%
triggers.quote: our backlog is a record $271 billion, up 25% year-over-year

triggers.label: Munitions capex ~$900M over 3 years
triggers.quote: where we've already invested nearly $900 million in CapEx over the last 3 years to expand capacity at these locations

triggers.label: Framework deals not yet finalised
triggers.quote: we're still going through the process to convert those into final agreements

guidance.quote: a new range of $92.5 billion to $93.5 billion, up from our prior range of $92 billion to $93 billion
We now see adjusted EPS of between $6.70 and $6.90 for the full year
we remain on track to our outlook of between $8.25 billion and $8.75 billion for the full year
We expect sales to grow high single digits on an adjusted and organic basis, up from our prior range of mid to high single digits
We now expect operating profit growth between $275 million and $375 million versus 2025

red_flags.label: Airbus GTF delivery negotiations ongoing
red_flags.quote: In terms of the discussions with Airbus, those are always ongoing.

red_flags.label: Negative GTF engine margins on new deliveries
red_flags.quote: We're going to continue to see negative margins on deliveries of new engines

evasions.quote: I don't want to get to too far into the details on this, Peter, only because we're still in the process of negotiations
And I have no doubt that we'll ultimately get there to where we need to be on volumes going forward.
